subject: science
passage: When Mimivirus was described in 2003, its particles were so large, roughly 400 nanometers across even without their surface fibers, that it had at first been mistaken for a bacterium. Its genome proved just as surprising, containing genes linked to protein synthesis, a process viruses were thought to leave entirely to their hosts. Such discoveries have not erased the distinction between viruses and cellular life, since Mimivirus still cannot reproduce outside a host cell, but they have made the boundary between the two look more ______ than the textbook dichotomy implied.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The text says the discoveries "have not erased the distinction" but have changed how the boundary looks compared with a strict "dichotomy." Features once thought to belong only to cells turned up in a virus, so the boundary now seems to let some traits cross it. "Porous" means allowing things to pass through, without implying that the boundary is gone.
explanation.A: Incorrect. An arbitrary boundary would be meaningless, but the text says the distinction has not been erased, because Mimivirus still depends on a host cell.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about the age of the boundary between viruses and cells.
explanation.C: Correct. A porous boundary still exists but lets some things cross it, just as cell-like traits appear in a virus that still "cannot reproduce outside a host cell."
explanation.D: Incorrect. The discoveries made the boundary seem less strict than the "textbook dichotomy," not more.
